clue.text: A hundred men nicely treated? Not with such treatment

definitions.note: clemency is merciful treatment, so harsh, unmerciful handling is its opposite

indicators.note: letters that are treated are processed and worked over, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A question whether a hundred men were handled politely, answered with a curt no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges C (a hundred) with MEN NICELY. The definition answers the surface question: men nicely treated would not get harsh handling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means harshness or a lack of mercy, the very opposite of being dealt with nicely.

clue.text: Wager, small, in pub is started but not finished

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, the bet and the small word sitting inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a bet is a wager
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A gambler places a little bet at the local, and the matter hangs half-done.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Wager' makes it look like a separate item, but the bet and 'small' both go into the pub, splitting it. The definition is the hyphenated phrase for something halfway done.
explanation.definitionFit: Something halfway along, begun but incomplete, is in an intermediate state.

clue.text: Indian detail to move very slowly

indicators.note: read as de-tail: the last letter, the word's tail, is cut off

parts.note: to creep is to move very slowly

explanation.surface: Some feature of India is said to move at a crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' looks like a noun meaning a small point; split it as de-tail, taking the tail off CREEP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a Native American people, so an Indian in the older North American sense.

clue.text: To stop rage and put in peril

parts.note: to end something is to stop it
anger is rage

explanation.surface: Calming someone's fury is said to be dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten something with harm is to expose it to danger.

clue.text: Moral standard of the thickest

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters from the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A principle held by the dimmest people.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'the' into 'thickest'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a principle of right conduct, a moral code.

clue.text: Engaged as assistant priest to restrain Catholic's lack of exactitude

indicators.note: the long phrase holds the extra letter inside it, as if restraining it

parts.note: a curate holds a curacy, so someone engaged as one is in a curacy

explanation.walkthrough: IN A CURACY (employed as a curate) takes C inside to give IN A C CURACY.

clue.text: A way of presentation that's far from straight

parts.note: a slant is the angle or bias given to a story

explanation.surface: A biased way of telling things is anything but honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying at an angle, on a slope, means not upright or level.

clue.text: See blonde suffering loss of vital fluid

indicators.note: the words are suffering, in a bad way, so their letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Look at the fair-haired woman in distress as she bleeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleeding from the nose loses blood, the fluid we cannot live without.

clue.text: Early brand of whisky?

parts.note: read 'Early' as Earl-y: the whisky brand shares its name with a famous Earl, the First World War commander, and is also one of the oldest whisky makers

explanation.surface: Asking after an old-established whisky label.
explanation.walkthrough: Haig whisky is an old Scottish brand; Field Marshal Earl Haig led the British army in the First World War, so 'Early' hints at the Earl.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Scotch whisky brand bearing the name of the soldier made an Earl after 1918.

clue.text: Talkative? That will change in Cyprus

indicators.note: the shuffled word goes in the country code, placed inside it

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus

indicators.note: the word 'That' will change its order of letters

explanation.surface: A gossip in Cyprus says a situation will alter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will change' is the anagram signal, and 'in' places the result inside the country code; 'Talkative?' is the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fond of conversation is chatty, inclined to talk a lot.

clue.text: Rob having to make reduction

definitions.meaning: to ... money is to deduct it from a price

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for stealing, and also means taking an amount off a bill.

clue.text: It's good for fellow leaving ancestor to come into assembly

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, good put in place of fellow

parts.note: a forefather is an ancestor

explanation.surface: A remark that a fine man departing from his forebear may join a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for fellow leaving' says G replaces F in FOREFATHER, giving FOREGATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather together in a meeting is to assemble.

clue.text: Made one? It's reversed

indicators.note: the little word It is turned round where it stands in the longer word

parts.note: joined into a single whole means united

explanation.surface: Asking whether something was joined, and being told it has been undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's reversed' acts on the clue word 'It' inside the joined word. The whole clue is also the definition: once joined, now undone.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosened or unfastened, the reverse of being knotted together.

clue.text: Embarked on career as Oxford menial

indicators.note: to career is to rush wildly, so letters on a career are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who set out on a working life as a college servant in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedmaker is a servant who cleans students' rooms at Oxford and Cambridge colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A college servant whose duties include tidying rooms is a lowly domestic employee.

clue.text: Periodical trial's disrupted for the master

parts.note: a mag, magazine, is a periodical

indicators.note: the word is disrupted, its letters thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A magazine's legal case was upset, for the boss's sake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges TRIALS to ISTRAL; the possessive 's counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what belongs to or befits a master, as in a masterly or authoritative manner.

clue.text: Change direction by holding company traitor

indicators.note: the pair of words holds the abbreviation between them

parts.note: to turn is to change direction
at can mean by, as in at the door

explanation.surface: A firm switching sides to betray its people.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who deserts his side, a betrayer.

explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges 'idea', 'originally' takes the first letter of 'department', and 'in' puts the new notion inside the university letters.

clue.text: Go back with Heather giving lecherous looks?

indicators.note: go back tells us to reverse the short word

parts.note: ling is a name for heather

explanation.surface: Returning with a woman named Heather, eyeing people lustfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is the common heather plant, not a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogling means staring at someone with amorous or lustful eyes.

clue.text: One civil engineer has wood in fridge

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
box is a hardwood tree

explanation.surface: An engineer keeps timber in a refrigerator.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is an old-fashioned name for a refrigerator.

clue.text: Early scramble in Goodwood start for young horse

indicators.note: the letters of the word are scrambled into a new order
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rush at the start of a Goodwood race for a young horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Goodwood is an English racecourse in Sussex. 'scramble' turns EARLY into YEARL, then IN and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse between one and two years old.

clue.text: Subject's fib, for example, shown up

parts.note: a fib is a lie

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means read upwards, so reversed

explanation.surface: A subject's small lie, as an instance, gets exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal terms the word can denote a vassal, one bound to serve a lord.

clue.text: A smell is rising

definitions.note: a verb form here, standing for the noun meaning a climb

parts.note: a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: A smell is going up.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb or upward movement is a going-up.

clue.text: Important people backed wide boy

indicators.note: backed means taken backwards, the abbreviation reversed

parts.note: VIPs are very important people

explanation.surface: Big shots supported a shady dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a flashy small-time crook.

clue.text: Tool misused in daze

indicators.note: the letters are misused, put to a wrong arrangement

explanation.surface: A tool used carelessly by someone stunned.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: Deliberately regarding, goal

parts.note: on means regarding, as in a talk on art
a purpose is a goal

explanation.surface: With regard to an aim, done intentionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Done intentionally, not by accident.

clue.text: Awfully active DJ taking on a learner's description of part of speech

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are badly arranged

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A frantic disc jockey takes on a trainee's account of grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges ACTIVE DJ into ADJECTIV, then A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to words that qualify nouns, a grammatical class.
